chapter: Europe 1933, New York Cotton Club, Hodges group
title: Whether Ellington ever fired anyone
summary: Brown insists leaders do let people go, and they discuss Lil Greenwood and Jimmy Hamilton leaving over doubling pay.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: But your account just now is the first time I've ever heard anyone tell of being fired by Duke Ellington. Do you know of anybody else he ever fired?
Oh sure. Sure. That's a fallacy.
Who else.
There may not be many, but there have been people fired. Oh well, you say I'm sorry -- I can't keep you on -- I can't keep you -- well that's firing.
Yeah, but I --
Well that's been done by everybody. There is no one -- you can't go by that angelic aura -- you know. Really, things are not like that.
Not angelic, I know that.
(Inaudible)

Yeah, you have to realize -- and some of them are perfectly logical and legal and right to be done. When a person is on your job and -- well we'll say some of them get too far out -- act in a bad fashion -- then you let them go for awhile. That's being fired.
Certainly --
So -- certain people that that's been done to.
remember him
I (Inaudible) like leaving Lil Greenwood without telling her the band was moving on. That was the way he left her. But he didn't tell her she was fired.
(Laughter) There's not much difference between leaving you with nothing and telling you you're fired is there?
No, but the actual act of speaking the words --
Yes, uh-huh.
-- he seemed to avoid whenever he could.
Right. Right. But --
Jimmy
Hamilton left the band for the
same reason you did. He was asked to double and he didn't get any extra money. But he quit. He didn't get fired.
He quit. Oh, he had a nice deal to go to. His wife was working in the Islands and they went down and worked together -- which is nice.
